title: Crispy Chow Mein with Chicken and Vegetables
summary: Thin egg noodles are fried into a crisp golden cake, then topped with a glossy chicken and vegetable stir-fry in a savoury soy sauce.
equipment: wok (35 cm) or large non-stick frying pan (30 cm)
small bowls for the prepared ingredients
flat plate the size of the pan

ingredients.item: fresh thin egg noodles (chow mein or Hong Kong-style)
fresh bean sprouts, rinsed and drained well
pak choi, leaves separated, halved lengthways
spring onions, cut into 4 cm lengths

steps.title: Cook and dry the noodles
steps.text: Bring 3 litres of unsalted water to the boil, add the noodles and loosen them with chopsticks, then cook for just 1 minute until flexible. Drain, rinse under cold water until cool, and shake off as much water as you can before tossing with 1 tsp of the oil and spreading them on a tray for 10 minutes. A dry surface is what lets the noodles crisp in the pan rather than steam.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Toss the sliced chicken breast with the soy sauce and cornflour and leave it while you prepare everything else. The thin cornflour coating seals in moisture during the hot, fast stir-fry, so the chicken stays juicy rather than drying out.

steps.title: Whisk the sauce
steps.text: Whisk together the stock, oyster sauce, light and dark soy sauces, cornflour, sesame oil and white pepper in a jug or bowl. Keep it close to the stove, as cornflour settles quickly and needs another whisk right before it goes in the pan.

steps.title: Fry the noodle cake
steps.text: Heat 2 tbsp of oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat, spread the noodles into an even layer and press them down firmly with a spatula. Fry undisturbed for 4-5 minutes until the base turns deep golden brown — resist the urge to move them, as constant stirring is what stops a crust forming.

steps.title: Flip and crisp the other side
steps.text: Slide the noodle cake onto a flat plate, then invert it back into the pan so the pale side is now facing down. Drizzle the last of the oil around the edge and fry for a further 3-4 minutes until that side is just as golden. Slide the finished cake onto a warm platter and set aside while you make the topping.

steps.title: Stir-fry the chicken
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp of oil in the wok over high heat and stir-fry the chicken for 3-4 minutes, until it's browned on the outside and no pink remains inside — check the thickest piece reaches 74°C. Lift it out onto a plate and set aside.

steps.title: Stir-fry the vegetables
steps.text: Add the remaining oil to the wok with the garlic and ginger and stir for 20 seconds until fragrant, then add the carrot and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add the pak choi stems for 1 minute, followed by the leaves, bean sprouts and spring onions for a final 30-45 seconds, until the sprouts are hot but still crunchy. Cooking the sturdier vegetables first and the leaves last keeps everything crisp-tender rather than overcooked.

steps.title: Add sauce and chicken
steps.text: Give the sauce another whisk, then pour it into the wok and stir until it comes to the boil and turns glossy and thickened, about 1 minute. Return the chicken to the pan and stir to coat everything evenly. The cornflour in the sauce is what gives it that glossy cling rather than a watery pool.

steps.title: Spoon over the noodle cake
steps.text: Bring the noodle cake to the table whole, then spoon the hot chicken and vegetable topping over it just before serving. The steam from the topping softens the top of the cake while the base stays crackling crisp underneath. Cut and serve straight away for the best contrast in texture.

tips: Don't stir the noodles while they're forming the cake — moving them too soon stops the crust from setting and you'll end up with a soft tangle instead of a crisp base.
Dry the noodles thoroughly before frying, as damp noodles steam instead of browning in the pan.
Whisk the sauce again just before it goes into the wok, since the cornflour sinks to the bottom while it waits.
safety: Check the chicken's thickest piece reaches 74°C with no pink showing before taking it out of the wok.
storage: Keep leftovers in a covered container in the fridge for up to 2 days, though the noodle cake will lose some crispness as it sits. Reheat in a hot frying pan or microwave until steaming hot throughout (at least 74°C). This dish isn't suitable for freezing, as the crisp texture doesn't survive thawing. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
